payload.goal: Registrar una factura de proveedor en Tripletex a partir del PDF adjunto, creando el proveedor si no existe, con cuenta de gasto 6300 e IVA de entrada 25%.
likely_resources: PDF de factura de proveedor adjunto
Endpoint de facturas de proveedor / supplier invoices de Tripletex
success_checks: Existe un proveedor con nombre Estrella SL y org.nr 886023979
La factura de proveedor INV-2026-6201 está registrada con fecha 2026-05-26
La fecha de vencimiento de la factura es 2026-06-25
La línea contable usa la cuenta 6300
La base imponible registrada es 54500 y el IVA de entrada es 13625 al 25%
El total de la factura registrada es 68125
La cuenta bancaria del proveedor 62014961092 queda guardada si el modelo de datos lo permite
risk_notes: No se especifica la entidad legal del comprador en Tripletex; puede requerirse seleccionar la compañía correcta.
El PDF no indica moneda explícita; se asume NOK por importes en kr.
La cuenta 6300 viene indicada en la factura, pero la validación contable depende del plan de cuentas de la empresa.
Puede ser necesario mapear el IVA de entrada al código fiscal exacto de Tripletex para 25%.
No se aporta referencia interna, departamento, proyecto ni centro de coste.
Si Tripletex exige número de proveedor único o país, esos datos no están explícitos.
ordered_steps: Buscar proveedor existente por organizationNumber=886023979 o name='Estrella SL' mediante endpoint de suppliers.
Si no existe, crear proveedor con nombre Estrella SL, organizationNumber 886023979, address 'Solveien 42, 3015 Drammen' y bankAccountNumber 62014961092 mediante endpoint de suppliers.
Validar que la cuenta contable 6300 existe y es utilizable para gasto en el plan de cuentas.
Resolver el código de IVA de entrada correspondiente al 25% en Tripletex.

Crear registro de factura de proveedor con supplierId, invoiceNumber 'INV-2026-6201', invoiceDate '2026-05-26', dueDate '2026-06-25', currency 'NOK' si aplica, y total 68125 mediante endpoint de supplier invoices.
Añadir línea de factura con descripción 'IT-konsulenttjenester', amountExcludingVat 54500, account 6300 y vatRate 25% o vatType de entrada equivalente.
Verificar que el IVA calculado/registrado es 13625 y el total 68125.
Guardar o confirmar la factura para que quede registrada en Tripletex.

planned_endpoints.summary: Create supplier. Related supplier addresses may also be created.
Find accounts corresponding with sent data.
Add new voucher. IMPORTANT: Also creates postings. Only the gross amounts will be used. Amounts should be rounded to 2 decimals.

rules: When email is provided, ALWAYS set BOTH email AND invoiceEmail to the same value.
ALWAYS include phoneNumber if provided in the prompt — scoring checks phone.
ALWAYS include postalAddress with addressLine1, postalCode, city, country={id: 161} when address info is provided.
ALWAYS set BOTH amountGross AND amountGrossCurrency to the SAME value on every posting.
Do NOT include postings with row=0 — row 0 is system-generated and will cause a 422.
When using vatType != 0 (e.g. VAT 25%), include ONLY the debit posting. Tripletex auto-generates VAT and credit postings.
For supplier invoices, set supplier={"id": supplier_id} on the debit posting.
For salary/payroll vouchers, set employee={"id": employee_id} on each posting.
Always resolve account numbers via GET /ledger/account?number=XXXX first, then use account={"id": resolved_id}.
Postings with vatType={"id":0} (exempt) can include both debit and credit lines manually.

payload.headline: Supplier created but invoice voucher failed 5/6 scoring checks despite successful API call
what_went_wrong: Only 1/6 checks passed (supplier creation). The voucher posting structure was incorrect — mixing vatType=1 on expense line with manual VAT/AP postings caused Tripletex to auto-generate extra entries, producing wrong balances.
The 3-posting approach (net on 6300 with vatType=1, manual 2710, manual 2400) likely resulted in duplicate VAT entries since vatType=1 already triggers auto-generation of the VAT posting.

First voucher attempt with single posting (amountGross=68125, vatType=1) failed with balance error, wasting one API call and revealing misunderstanding of how Tripletex handles vatType auto-splitting.
The GET /ledger/account was called twice unnecessarily (parallel calls for 2400 and 2710 accounts) when a single call with query params could have retrieved both.
what_worked: Supplier 'Estrella SL' was created correctly with org.nr, bank account, and address (Check 1 passed).
VAT type resolution was correct — vatType id=1 is confirmed as 25% input VAT (Fradrag inngående avgift, høy sats).
what_to_try_next: Use a single expense posting with vatType=1 and amountGross=68125 (gross), plus only a credit posting on account 2400 for -68125 with vatType=0 and supplier reference — let Tripletex auto-split the VAT from the gross amount.
Alternatively, use 3 manual postings all with vatType=0: debit 6300 for 54500, debit 2710 for 13625, credit 2400 for -68125 — no auto-generation interference.
Eliminate the GET /ledger/vatType call (unnecessary verification) and combine the two GET /ledger/account calls into one to reduce total calls from 7 to 4-5.
unnecessary_calls: GET /ledger/vatType — used only to verify vatType id=1, which was already known from account's legalVatTypes list
Second GET /ledger/account (for account 2710) — could have been combined with first GET /ledger/account call using query params
First POST /ledger/voucher with single posting amountGross=68125 — incorrect structure that predictably failed balance validation
